up.name: MARVELL TECHNOLOGY INC
up.company_description: Marvell Technology designs custom AI chips (XPUs), networking silicon, and optical interconnects for hyperscale data centers. Semiconductor sector.
bullets: May 27 2026: Q1 FY27 earnings beat — revenue $2.418B (+28% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $0.80 vs. $0.75 consensus; Q2 guidance of $2.7B (+35% YoY) exceeded expectations.
Jun 2 2026: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang appeared on Marvell's Computex 2026 stage in Taipei, calling it 'the next trillion-dollar company' — stock surged ~32% that session, closing at ~$290.
Marvell launched the Teralynx T100 switch chip (102.4 Tbps) at Computex, claiming 25% lower power vs. competition, reinforcing its AI networking infrastructure position.
Custom silicon (XPU) revenue hit $1.5B in FY26; management guided 20%+ growth in FY27 with 20+ new AI chip design wins entering production in FY28–FY29.
Nvidia simultaneously announced a $2B strategic investment in Marvell, cementing the hyperscaler partnership narrative and validating the custom silicon roadmap.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Q1 FY27 earnings beat plus Jensen Huang's 'next trillion-dollar company' endorsement at Computex on June 2.

up.name: HEWLETT PACKARD ENTERPRISE
up.company_description: Hewlett Packard Enterprise sells AI and traditional servers, networking equipment (Juniper Networks), and hybrid cloud infrastructure to enterprises. Information Technology sector.
bullets: Jun 1 2026: Q2 FY26 earnings blowout — revenue $10.68B (+40% YoY), beating $9.79B consensus by ~$900M; swung to $624M net income vs. prior-year loss.
Server segment revenue $5.45B (+32.7% YoY), ~$800M ahead of estimates; Networking (Juniper) $2.7B (+148.2% YoY) as the full-quarter Juniper consolidation landed.
FY26 revenue growth guidance raised to 29–33% (from prior 17–22%); Q3 revenue guided $11.5–12.1B with non-GAAP EPS $0.88–0.93.

May 29 2026 (pre-earnings): Dell reported record Q1 FY27 revenue of $43.8B (+88% YoY) and raised AI-Optimized Server forecast to ~$60B; HPE closed up 12.76% in sympathy that day as investors anticipated a similar beat.
HPE raised networking revenue growth outlook to 72–75% for FY26 (from 68–73%), signaling durable Juniper synergies beyond the initial acquisition step-up.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Dell's May 29 sympathy rally followed by HPE's own blowout Q2 FY26 earnings on June 1, beating revenue estimates by ~$900M.

up.name: DELL TECHNOLOGIES INC CLASS C
up.company_description: Dell Technologies sells servers, storage and PCs, increasingly AI-optimized data-center systems to enterprises and hyperscalers; an Information Technology (hardware) company earning on volume and services.
bullets: [2026-05-28] Reported Q1 FY27 (quarter ended May 1) after-hours: revenue $43.84B, up 88% YoY, a sizable beat; stock gapped up ~33% the next session.
[2026-05-28] AI-optimized server revenue hit a record $16.1B, up 757% YoY; booked $24.4B of AI orders and exited with a record $51.3B AI backlog.
[2026-05-28] Raised FY27 AI-server revenue target to $60B and total revenue guide to $165-169B (~47% growth at midpoint), driving the beat-and-raise.
[2026-05-29] Print became the anchor of a broad AI-infrastructure rally — read across lifted SMCI, HPE and memory names (MU) as proof hyperscaler AI server spend is accelerating.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Sell-side target hikes and follow-through on the print; watch any commentary on AI-server margins and backlog conversion at upcoming conferences.

up.name: OKTA INC CLASS A
up.company_description: Okta sells subscription identity and access-management software (workforce and customer login/security) to enterprises; Information Technology (software/cybersecurity).
bullets: [2026-05-28] Q1 FY27 print: revenue $765M (+11% YoY) vs $752M est, adj EPS $0.91 vs $0.85 est; cRPO $2.499B (+12%); DBNRR inflected up to 107%; FCF $271M (35% margin).

[2026-05-28] Raised FY27 revenue guide to $3.185-3.205B (+9-10%); Q2 guide $790-794M — management leaned into agentic AI forcing enterprises to buy identity-security tooling, with a 'record pipeline.'
[2026-05-29] Posted a record ~30% single-day gain Friday, the standout in a software group reset by Snowflake's and Okta's beats; read as the 'replacement risk to AI-enablement trade' rotation.
[2026-05-29] Part of the broadest software re-rating since 2001 (software ETF +21% for May) — peers ServiceNow, Atlassian, Workday, Asana and Shopify each rallied double-digits in sympathy.
up.ten_day_catalyst: May 28 Q1 beat with a raised guide and an agentic-AI identity narrative drove a record one-day surge.

up.name: TWILIO INC CLASS A
up.company_description: Twilio provides a cloud communications platform (SMS, voice, email, video APIs) that lets companies embed messaging and engagement into their products; earns usage-based and subscription revenue from developers and enterprises.
bullets: June 1 surge: TWLO jumped +19.4% in a single session as Wall Street revisited the raised 2026 outlook from Q1 earnings (April 30); multiple analysts lifted targets into a $200–$250 band, with Bank of America upgrading to Buy and raising its target from $110 to $190.

Q1 2026 results (April 30): revenue $1.41B (+20% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $0.59 vs. $0.39 est. (+51% beat); net income $90.1M vs. a net loss in the prior-year period — the magnitude of the earnings beat had been underappreciated at the initial reaction.
Full-year 2026 guidance raised: revenue growth lifted to 14%–15% from prior 11.5%–12.5%; non-GAAP operating income guided to ~$1.0–$1.1B, signalling the profitability inflection is ahead of schedule.

AI pivot narrative: Gartner named Twilio a Leader in CPaaS for 2026 (highest in Ability to Execute); the SIGNAL conference in early May introduced AI agent-native voice and messaging workflows, repositioning TWLO from a 'messaging tollbooth' to AI engagement infrastructure.

Snowflake-ignited software sector rally (May 28–29) created the backdrop; Motley Fool specifically cited TWLO as one of the biggest winners in the software catch-up trade, with the stock up ~19% on June 1 alongside MongoDB and HubSpot.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Delayed recognition of Q1 FY2026 earnings beat (EPS +51% vs. est.) and guidance raise, amplified by broad software sector re-rating and multiple analyst target upgrades on Jun 1.

up.name: NETAPP INC
up.company_description: NetApp sells hybrid cloud data storage hardware and software, helping enterprises manage data across on-premise and public cloud environments; revenue from product sales and recurring support/subscription contracts.
bullets: Q4 FY2026 earnings (reported May 28, 2026): revenue $1.948B for the quarter and $6.925B for full-year FY26; non-GAAP EPS $2.43 vs. consensus $2.19 — a ~11% beat on the bottom line.
FY2027 guidance raised materially: management guided revenue $7.325B–$7.575B and non-GAAP EPS $8.70–$9.00, both ahead of the Street, with the margin expansion narrative intact.

All-flash array revenue hit $4.2B in FY26 (+11% YoY) and a multiyear Google Cloud agreement drove product revenue up 14% YoY to $966M in Q4 — concrete hyperscaler-linked demand proof that lifted the AI infrastructure angle.
Public cloud revenue reached $688M for FY26 (+18% YoY), demonstrating the shift toward recurring software/subscription mix that commands higher multiples.

Snowflake's +36% session on May 28 (same reporting day) catalysed a sector-wide re-rating of cloud infrastructure names; NetApp's own earnings beat landed on the same day, amplifying the move as generalist buyers rotated into the group.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Q4 FY2026 earnings beat (EPS $2.43 vs. $2.19 est.) and FY2027 guidance raise, reported May 28 on the same day as Snowflake's blowout.

up.name: CDW CORP
up.company_description: CDW is a US IT solutions reseller selling hardware, software and services to business, government and education customers, earning gross margin on product sales plus higher-margin services. GICS Information Technology.
bullets: JPMorgan upgraded CDW from Neutral to Overweight on May 27, 2026, citing renewed growth conviction after Q1 revenue of $5.68B beat the ~$5.48B estimate.
NVIDIA's late-May unveiling of the RTX Spark chip for AI-enabled Windows PCs framed CDW as a beneficiary of a coming corporate PC-refresh cycle, lifting shares.
Director David W. Nelms bought 18,000 shares for ~$2.0M on May 27, 2026, a high-profile insider signal during the run.
A $1B share-repurchase authorization increase in mid-May added a capital-return tailwind compounding the move to roughly +20% over the 5d window.
up.ten_day_catalyst: May 27 JPMorgan Overweight upgrade plus NVIDIA RTX Spark AI-PC refresh narrative and insider buying.

up.name: RIVIAN AUTOMOTIVE INC CLASS A
up.company_description: Rivian designs and builds premium electric SUVs, pickups and commercial delivery vans, earning revenue from vehicle sales plus software and services. GICS Consumer Discretionary (autos).
bullets: Rivian's R2 SUV launch was set for June 9, 2026 (~$58,000), with late-May order invitations and demo drives driving buyer interest and the rally.
Volkswagen deepened its strategic stake via a ~$1B private placement of 62.89M new shares, lifting VW to ~209.8M Class A shares (~15.9% of float), validating Rivian.
Q1 2026 results beat: adjusted EPS of ~-$0.55 topped the -$0.60 consensus, revenue $1.38B (+11%), deliveries +20% YoY, software/services +~50%.
Management's 2026 delivery guide of 62,000-67,000 vehicles underpinned the ~+19% move into the R2 launch over the 5d window.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Imminent June 9 R2 SUV launch plus Volkswagen's ~$1B capital injection and stake increase.

up.name: CLOUDFLARE INC CLASS A
up.company_description: Cloudflare operates a global cloud network platform (CDN, Zero Trust security, DDoS protection, developer compute) for enterprises; earns subscription revenue that scales with customer seat count and traffic volume.
bullets: Anthropic partnership announced in the window: Cloudflare launched 'Cloudflare Environments for Claude Managed Agents', providing secure sandboxed infrastructure for AI agents — directly tying the company to the fastest-growing workload type and prompting a re-rating of its AI infrastructure value.
May 29 alone: NET closed +6.15%; RBC Capital reiterated Outperform and raised its price target, citing AI agent traffic as an incremental demand driver not yet in consensus models.
Sector tailwind: Snowflake's +36% session on May 28 ignited a broader software rally; the WisdomTree Cloud Computing Fund (WCLD) surged ~9% on May 29, lifting all high-multiple cloud names.

Q1 2026 results (reported May 7, before the window): revenue $639.8M (+34% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $0.25 vs. $0.17 est. — the prior beat had already set a strong foundation; the Anthropic news gave investors a second catalyst to add to positions.
Annual Investor Day scheduled June 9, 2026 created incremental buy-ahead demand as investors anticipated updated long-term targets and potential AI monetisation disclosures.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Anthropic AI agent partnership announcement plus sector-wide cloud software re-rating following Snowflake's May 28 blowout earnings.

up.name: AXON ENTERPRISE INC
up.company_description: Axon makes Tasers, body cameras and a cloud software/evidence platform for law enforcement and public safety, monetized via hardware plus high-margin recurring SaaS subscriptions. GICS Industrials.
bullets: Shares jumped ~12.8% on May 28, 2026 to $441.25, coinciding with Axon's annual shareholder meeting and a May 27 presentation at TD Cowen's TMT Conference.
Renewed enthusiasm over AI product revenue up ~700% YoY and Dedrone counter-drone revenue up ~300% in Q1 2026 fueled the bullish narrative.
Axon raised its full-year 2026 growth outlook to 30%-32%, a delayed but powerful digestion of the May 6 Q1 print.
A new May 2026 partnership with radar specialist Echodyne (MESA radar into Axon Air/Dedrone) reinforced the counter-drone growth story, contributing to the ~+17% week.
up.ten_day_catalyst: May 27-28 investor events (TD Cowen, AGM) crystallizing AI/counter-drone growth and raised 30-32% FY guidance.

down.name: AST SPACEMOBILE INC CLASS A
down.company_description: AST SpaceMobile builds a space-based cellular broadband network enabling direct-to-device satellite connectivity for standard smartphones. Earns revenue via carrier contracts. Communication Services sector.
bullets: May 29, 2026: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket exploded on its LC-36A launch pad at Cape Canaveral overnight May 28-29; ASTS fell ~15-18% that day from an all-time high of $133.86 hit May 28.
Blue Origin launchpad damage assessed as severe — NASA's Isaacman noted restoration could take until 2028, pushing ASTS's larger constellation launch window from Q4 2026 toward Q1 2027.
Deutsche Bank downgraded ASTS to Hold (PT cut to $106 from $117) on June 1-2, citing the delayed coverage timeline; Bernstein-linked analysts also flagged a 2028 coverage timeline shift.

AST clarified its near-term BlueBird 8-10 launch is on a SpaceX Falcon 9 (not Blue Origin) and its satellites are launcher-agnostic, limiting direct operational impact — but sentiment and timeline credibility took the hit.
Sector read-across: Planet Labs also dropped ~8% on May 29; broader space-sector de-rating on launch-infrastructure risk.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded May 28-29, delaying ASTS constellation timeline and triggering analyst downgrade.

down.name: PVH CORP
down.company_description: PVH owns the Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger apparel brands, earning revenue from global wholesale and direct-to-consumer sales plus licensing. GICS Consumer Discretionary.
bullets: Despite Q1 2026 EPS of $2.01 beating the $1.82 forecast on ~$2B revenue, the stock plunged ~20-22% on weak forward guidance.
PVH cut its FY revenue outlook to down slightly on a constant-currency basis, versus prior flat-to-slightly-up, triggering the sell-off.
CEO Stefan Larsson attributed the cut to fallout from the war in Iran hitting Middle East sales, with knock-on effects in Turkey and higher fuel prices pressuring European demand.
Analysts flagged that the EPS guide leaned on ~$100M in tariff-related benefit, raising doubts about underlying earnings quality and deepening the ~-19% move.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Q1 2026 guidance cut (revenue now down slightly) on Iran-war Middle East/Turkey/Europe demand hit, despite the EPS beat.

down.name: ROCKET LAB CORP
down.company_description: Rocket Lab builds and launches small rockets (Electron) and spacecraft components; earns revenue from launch services and space systems. GICS: Industrials.
bullets: June 1, 2026: RKLB fell ~14.8% in a single session after a Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a static fire test at Cape Canaveral on May 28, triggering a broad space-sector selloff — AST SpaceMobile, Planet Labs and Intuitive Machines each fell 5%+.

Blue Origin's sole New Glenn launchpad (LC-36) was so severely damaged that NASA Administrator Isaacman said restoration could extend to 2028, raising investor fears about sector-wide launch delays and satellite constellation timelines.

RKLB had already risen to a 52-week high of $150.23 in mid-May on eight record closes, leaving the stock technically overbought and vulnerable to profit-taking; the sector catalyst accelerated the reversal.
May 20, 2026: Rocket Lab entered an at-the-market equity offering to raise up to $3 billion in common stock, stoking shareholder dilution concerns a week before the explosion.
Four RKLB insiders collectively sold $18 million of stock at or near the May highs, adding negative sentiment headlines to the dilution and explosion news.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Blue Origin New Glenn rocket explosion June 1 triggered broad space-sector selloff, compounded by RKLB's $3B equity offering dilution fears.

down.name: KARMAN HOLDINGS INC
down.company_description: Karman Holdings makes mission-critical components for defense and space systems (propulsion, payload protection, missiles), selling to primes and government; recently IPO'd, GICS Industrials.
bullets: [2026-05-29] Karman priced an upsized underwritten secondary offering of 14,000,000 shares by selling stockholders at $61.00, below market, driving a ~10% one-day drop on added supply.
[2026-05-20] KeyBanc cut its target to $100 from $122 (Overweight) on higher near-term investment and integration costs after Q1.
[2026-05-19] Piper Sandler trimmed its target to $114 from $127 (Overweight).
[2026-05-12] Q1 FY26 print showed revenue $151.2M and EPS $0.11 missing estimates despite a record $1.0B backlog and raised FY guidance; stock fell ~7% the next morning.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Post-offering supply absorption and whether the discounted deal price acts as a near-term floor or ceiling will drive the next move.

down.name: BULLISH
down.company_description: Bullish operates a regulated cryptocurrency exchange; earns trading fees and financial-services revenue. Recently expanding into blockchain-enabled equity transfer-agent services. GICS: Financials.
bullets: June 1, 2026: BLSH fell ~7.8% in a single session, continuing the selloff triggered by dual negative catalysts from the prior week — Q1 earnings miss and the Equiniti acquisition announcement.
May 14, 2026: BLSH fell ~6% after Q1 2026 results missed consensus — adjusted EPS of $0.13 vs. $0.17 expected, revenue $92.8M vs. ~$95M expected — signalling weak exchange trading volumes.

May 5, 2026: BLSH dropped ~8.5% in pre-market after announcing a $4.2 billion acquisition of Equiniti (a transfer agent), funded primarily with ~$2.35B in BLSH stock at $38.48/share VWAP — heavily dilutive and execution-risky ahead of a January 2027 close.
Bitcoin fell from ~$75,850 intra-week to ~$66,650 by June 3 (down ~12%), reducing crypto-exchange trading volumes and fee revenue expectations for the sector.

Despite the decline, 11 analysts maintain a consensus Buy rating with a $48.65 average price target (+65% from June levels), suggesting the market views the reaction as excessive rather than fundamental deterioration.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Q1 earnings miss combined with residual selloff from the $4.2B Equiniti all-stock acquisition announcement weighed on the 5d window.

down.name: COTY INC CLASS A
down.company_description: Coty is a global beauty company selling prestige and consumer fragrances, cosmetics and skincare (e.g., Calvin Klein, Gucci licenses, CoverGirl), earning revenue from branded product sales. GICS Consumer Staples.
bullets: COTY fell to a fresh 52-week low of ~$1.95 in the window, extending a slide that has cut the stock ~61% over the past year amid no new positive catalyst.
Overhang persisted from the Dec 12, 2025 abrupt CEO Sue Nabi departure and the Feb 5, 2026 withdrawal of FY2026 guidance plus >70% drop in Consumer Beauty operating income.

A wave of securities class-action 'final deadline' investor-alert press releases clustered around the May 22, 2026 lead-plaintiff deadline (class period May 7, 2025-Feb 4, 2026), keeping sentiment negative into the window.
Analysts (TD Cowen, Wells Fargo, Goldman, Canaccord at ~$2.50 PT) had cut targets on inventory destocking and an EBITDA estimate cut from ~$1B toward ~$836M, sustaining the ~-17% decline.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Continued post-CEO-exit / withdrawn-guidance overhang plus litigation 'deadline' noise pushed COTY to a fresh 52-week low; no single new catalyst.

down.name: CBOE GLOBAL MARKETS INC
down.company_description: Cboe Global Markets operates options, futures, equities and FX exchanges, earning transaction fees, market-data and access fees; GICS Financials.
bullets: [2026-05] The 5-day decline appears valuation/positioning-driven rather than news-driven: CBOE had run ~49% over the prior year and traded ~47% above one fair-value estimate (~$333 vs ~$226) before the pullback.
[2026-05-28] News flow was actually constructive, with SEC approval to offer extended (pre/post-market) trading hours for select multi-listed single-stock options starting July 13.
[2026-05-18] Cboe expanded its DJX index-options suite with daily-expiring options, extending its 0DTE franchise (0DTE hit a record ~50% of index-options volume in Q1).

[2026-05] Management had raised FY26 organic net-revenue growth guidance to low-double-digit/mid-teens from mid-single-digit, so the sell-off looks like a high-multiple momentum unwind, not a fundamental deterioration.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Monthly options/futures volume data and whether the high-multiple momentum unwind extends or stabilizes will drive the near-term move.

down.name: UWM HOLDINGS CORP CLASS A
down.company_description: UWM Holdings is the largest US wholesale mortgage lender, originating loans through independent brokers and earning gain-on-sale and servicing income. GICS: Financials.
bullets: On May 30, 2026 (vote previously scheduled), Two Harbors' board again backed CrossCountry Mortgage's $12.00/share cash deal and rejected UWMC's competing $12.50 proposal, leaving UWMC's bid stalled and the acquisition path uncertain.
Two Harbors stockholders/board adjourned the CCM merger vote a second time into June, pushing it to June 11, 2026, prolonging the contested-bid overhang on UWMC shares.

The stock was already weak heading into the window, down roughly 26% over the prior month and trading near $2.92 as of mid/late May 2026, reflecting failed-acquisition and strategic-direction concerns.

Goldman Sachs cut its UWM Holdings price target to $5 from $6, reinforcing the negative sentiment as the depressed-housing/low-origination backdrop pressured the wholesale-lending model into early June 2026.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Continued setback in UWMC's contested bid for Two Harbors (board rejection, vote adjourned to June 11) plus a Goldman price-target cut.

down.name: CELSIUS HOLDINGS INC
down.company_description: Celsius Holdings sells fitness/energy drinks (Celsius, Alani Nu, Rockstar via PepsiCo distribution), earning revenue on branded ready-to-drink beverages. GICS: Consumer Staples.
bullets: On June 3, 2026, the Texas Attorney General opened an investigation into Celsius' Alani Nu energy drinks over marketing aimed at teens, and the stock fell about 7% on the news.
The regulatory probe hit the acquisition (Alani Nu) that has been carrying Celsius' growth, after Q1 2026 showed core Celsius brand revenue up only ~6% with most growth from Alani Nu and Rockstar.
Margin worries compounded the slide: Q1 (quarter ended March 2026) gross margin fell to 48.3% from 52.3% a year earlier on higher aluminum and freight costs.
The June 2, 2026 dbAccess/Deutsche Bank Consumer Conference appearance (management touting stabilization) failed to offset the AG-investigation hit the next day, leaving the 5-day window net down.
down.ten_day_catalyst: June 3, 2026 Texas AG investigation into Alani Nu's teen-targeted marketing drove a ~7% drop, with margin/core-growth worries amplifying the decline.

down.name: CIRCLE INTERNET GROUP INC CLASS A
down.company_description: Circle Internet Group issues the USDC stablecoin, earning reserve interest income (largely on Treasuries) and sharing it with distributors like Coinbase. GICS: Information Technology.
bullets: On June 3, 2026, CoinDesk reported Coinbase is weighing joining a competing Stripe/Visa/Mastercard stablecoin platform; CRCL fell as much as ~4% at the open on the threat to its distribution relationship.
The report raised fears around the Coinbase–Circle USDC revenue-share agreement up for renewal in August 2026, where Coinbase could gain leverage and squeeze Circle's economics further.
A broad crypto risk-off move pressured crypto equities in the window, with Bitcoin sliding below ~$67,000 after a ~$1.8B liquidation wave (down ~2.8% on the day).

On June 2, 2026 the stock fell ~3.92% (from $104.97 to $100.85); shares fell in 6 of the prior 10 days (~-9.5%), extending a decline of ~23% since the May 11 pivot top, layered on a persistent USDC gross-margin/distribution-cost overhang.
down.ten_day_catalyst: June 3 report that Coinbase may join a rival Stripe/Visa/Mastercard stablecoin platform, threatening Circle's distribution, amid a broad crypto selloff.

up.name: ENPHASE ENERGY INC
up.company_description: Enphase makes microinverters and battery systems for residential and commercial solar, earning hardware revenue plus US manufacturing tax credits; GICS Information Technology.
bullets: [2026-05-13] Spiked ~10-13% after opening US pre-orders for its IQ9S-3P commercial microinverter, letting customers safe-harbor gear ahead of tax-credit deadlines and pull forward demand.

[2026-05] Backdrop was a tough residential market: Q1 revenue $282.9M (sales -21% YoY) after the residential ITC expired end-2025, but adj EPS $0.47 beat and Q2 guide ($280-310M) bracketed the Street.
[2026-05-27] Rose ~8% as Enphase detailed a 1.25 MW IQ Solid-State Transformer aimed at AI data centers (demos 2026, pilots 2027), opening a new growth narrative beyond rooftop solar.
[2026-05-27] Roth Capital raised its target to $85 (from $55) and named ENPH a top 2026 pick on diversification into power infrastructure and data-center SSTs.
[2026-05] Distinct from the AI-hardware names: a solar story driven by new commercial product, tax-credit safe-harboring and an opportunistic AI-data-center pivot, not server demand.
up.ten_day_catalyst: A new commercial microinverter launch, a beat-and-bracket Q1, and an AI-data-center solid-state-transformer pivot (with a Roth upgrade) drove the run.

up.name: MARVELL TECHNOLOGY INC
up.company_description: Marvell Technology designs custom AI chips (XPUs), networking silicon, and optical interconnects for hyperscale data centers. Semiconductor sector.
bullets: The 20-day window spans a pre-earnings run-up (early May), the May 27 Q1 FY27 earnings beat ($2.418B revenue, +28% YoY; EPS $0.80 vs. $0.75 est.), and the Jun 2 Computex catalyst.
Stock was up ~100% year-to-date entering May 2026, driven by successive earnings beats and rising AI custom silicon revenue — strong prior momentum made the 20d base relatively low.
Jun 2: Jensen Huang's on-stage endorsement ('next trillion-dollar company') and the Nvidia $2B strategic investment added the blow-off leg, pushing market cap toward ~$250B.
FY27 and FY28 revenue outlook raised materially on earnings call: management cited 800G/1.6T optics, 51.2T Ethernet switches, and scale-up optical interconnects as growth drivers.
Broader AI semiconductor sector tailwinds: Dell's blowout May 28 earnings (+88% revenue) lifted all AI infrastructure stocks, providing sector cover for Marvell's pre-earnings move.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Compounded earnings beat (May 27) plus Jensen Huang's 'next trillion-dollar' Computex endorsement (Jun 2) across the full window.

up.name: HEWLETT PACKARD ENTERPRISE
up.company_description: Hewlett Packard Enterprise sells AI and traditional servers, networking equipment (Juniper Networks), and hybrid cloud infrastructure to enterprises. Information Technology sector.
bullets: The 20-day window (May 5–Jun 3) captured a slow build through mid-May, then two sharp step-ups: Dell sympathy (+12.76% on May 29) and the Jun 1 earnings beat (+25–36% on the day).
Dell's May 28 blowout — $43.8B revenue (+88% YoY), $51B AI server backlog, FY forecast for ~$60B AI-Optimized Server revenue — reset AI infrastructure demand expectations sector-wide.
HPE's own Q2 report on Jun 1 confirmed the demand: $10.68B revenue vs. $9.79B est., server revenue $5.45B ($800M beat), Networking $2.7B (+148% YoY on Juniper consolidation).
FY26 outlook upgraded to 29–33% revenue growth from 17–22% prior guidance, a massive revision that surprised buy-side models calibrated to a slower Juniper ramp.
Super Micro Computer (SMCI) also rose ~5% on Jun 2 in sympathy with HPE's print, confirming the sector rotation into AI server infrastructure names throughout the 20d window.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Dell's blowout AI server earnings sparked a sector rally on May 29; HPE's own record Q2 FY26 beat confirmed the AI server demand surge on June 1.

up.name: DELL TECHNOLOGIES INC CLASS C
up.company_description: Dell makes PCs and servers, increasingly AI-optimized data-center servers and storage sold to enterprises and hyperscalers; GICS Information Technology.
bullets: [2026-05-22] Surged ~15% intraday to ~$290 leading a broad AI-server rally (HPE +9%, SMCI +5%) into Nvidia's print, on positioning ahead of earnings.
[2026-05-28] Reported Q1 FY27: record revenue $43.8B (+88% YoY); AI-optimized server revenue $16.1B, up 757% YoY; adj EPS $4.86 vs ~$2.94 est.
[2026-05-28] Booked $24.4B AI orders and disclosed a record $51.3B AI backlog; raised FY27 AI-server revenue target to $60B.
[2026-05-29] Stock jumped ~32% for its best day ever as FY27 revenue guide was lifted to $165-169B and non-GAAP EPS to ~$17.90.
[2026-05] Part of the shared AI-infrastructure rally (with MU/SMCI) but the standout on its own blowout beat-and-raise.
up.ten_day_catalyst: A late-May AI-server beat-and-raise (AI server revenue +757% YoY, FY27 guide hiked) capping a month-long AI-infra rally.

up.name: SNOWFLAKE INC
up.company_description: Snowflake runs a consumption-priced cloud data platform for storing, querying and AI-analyzing enterprise data; GICS Information Technology.
bullets: [2026-05-27] Reported Q1 FY27 after close: product revenue $1.33B (+34% YoY, strongest sequential dollar growth ever); total revenue $1.39B beat $1.32B consensus; adj EPS $0.39 vs $0.32 est.
[2026-05-27] Raised FY27 product-revenue guide to ~$5.84B (~31% growth); RPO $9.21B (+38%); net revenue retention 126%.
[2026-05-27] Announced a ~$6B multi-year AWS commitment, framed by the Street as an inflection moment for AI workloads.
[2026-05-27] Disclosed a definitive deal to acquire Natoma, an enterprise MCP platform for AI agents, reinforcing the Cortex/AI narrative.
[2026-05-28] Stock spiked ~36-37%, its biggest single-day gain in years, on the AI-fueled beat and AWS megadeal.
up.ten_day_catalyst: A late-May Q1 beat-and-raise plus a ~$6B AWS commitment and an AI-agent acquisition drove the biggest single-day pop in years.

up.name: DATADOG INC CLASS A
up.company_description: Datadog sells usage-based cloud observability and security SaaS (monitoring, logs, APM, SIEM) to enterprises; GICS Information Technology.
bullets: [2026-05-07] Blowout Q1 print drove a ~30% single-day gap up: revenue $1.006B (+32% YoY), first $1B quarter, beating the $951-961M guide; non-GAAP EPS $0.60 vs ~$0.50 cons; total ARR topped $4B.

[2026-05-07] Raised FY26 revenue guide to $4.30-4.34B (+25-27%) from $4.06-4.10B, and Q2 to $1.07-1.08B implying the largest sequential dollar add in company history; agentic-AI demand and accelerating non-AI cohort (mid-20s%) cited.
[2026-05-07] Also won FedRAMP High authorization, widening federal TAM, adding to the bullish read.

[2026-05] DDOG led the broader software/observability leg of the cyber-software rally; its print was the single biggest catalyst of the batch and set the tone for the complex (CIBR ETF +~25% on the month).
[2026-05-30] Continued grinding to records as analysts re-rated the name post-print; shares had more than doubled off recent lows on AI-monitoring tailwinds.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Momentum from the Q1 beat plus agentic-AI/observability demand and the sector re-rating; no new print due near term.

up.name: ASTERA LABS INC
up.company_description: Fabless semiconductor company; designs PCIe, CXL, and AI fabric connectivity chips for hyperscale data centers and AI clusters. Information Technology.
bullets: May 5, 2026: Q1 2026 earnings reported — revenue of $308.4 million, up 93% YoY and ~5.5% above consensus of ~$292 million; non-GAAP EPS of $0.61 beat estimates by ~239%; gross margin 76.4%, up 150 bps YoY.
Q2 2026 guidance of $355–$365 million implies 15–18% sequential growth, well above Street expectations, driven by PCIe 6 ramp and early Scorpio X-Series scale-up fabric switch shipments.
Scorpio X-Series (320-lane AI fabric switch) launched with initial shipments; management guided it to become the largest product line by end of FY2026, up from ~15% of revenue in FY2025.

May 19, 2026: Astera Labs presented at J.P. Morgan Global Tech, Media & Communications Conference, reinforcing the AI connectivity growth story; Evercore ISI raised price target to $297 from $215, maintaining Outperform.

June 2–5, 2026: Computex 2026 in Taiwan — Astera hosted press events and live demos showcasing rack-scale AI connectivity strategy and collaborations with leading AI platform providers, sustaining momentum through end of window.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Q1 revenue +93% YoY with Q2 guidance 15–18% sequential growth; Scorpio AI fabric switch ramp and Computex catalyst extended the rally.

up.name: FORTINET INC
up.company_description: Fortinet sells cybersecurity and secure-networking products (FortiGate appliances, software, subscriptions/services), earning product and recurring subscription revenue. GICS: Information Technology.
bullets: On May 6, 2026 Fortinet reported Q1 2026: revenue $1.85B (+20.1% YoY) vs ~$1.77B est., non-GAAP EPS $0.82 vs $0.62 consensus, and ~31% billings growth — a clear beat-and-raise.

Product revenue jumped 41% to $645M as enterprises bought high-performance FortiGate appliances to secure AI data centers and OT environments; record non-GAAP operating margin of 35.8% and $1.01B free cash flow in the quarter.
Management raised FY2026 guidance to $7.71B–$7.87B revenue and $3.10–$3.16 EPS, signaling sustained growth and margin expansion.
Shares gapped from a $89.95 close on May 6 to above $105, peaking ~$111.80 intraday and closing near $110.47 on May 7, 2026, with a further ~5% gain on May 8 — driving the 20-day surge.
up.ten_day_catalyst: May 6, 2026 Q1 beat-and-raise (rev +20%, EPS $0.82 vs $0.62, product +41%) plus lifted FY26 guidance triggered the gap-up rally.

up.name: SAILPOINT INC
up.company_description: SailPoint provides identity security/governance software (SaaS), managing and securing user and machine/AI-agent access for enterprises on a subscription model. GICS: Information Technology.
bullets: On May 21, 2026 SailPoint announced an integration with the Claude Compliance API (and its Agentic Fabric solution for securing AI agents at scale), positioning it on the AI-agent identity-security theme and driving an ~8% pop.
Analyst support clustered in the window: Roth Capital initiated Buy on May 19, 2026 and Wells Fargo rated Buy on May 20, 2026, with a 16-analyst Buy consensus by May 20.
In early June 2026 Barclays raised its SAIL price target to $22 from $16, reinforcing upward momentum into the close of the 20-day window.
FY2026 revenue of $1.07B (+24.4% YoY from $861.6M) underpinned the rally, with the next earnings report set for June 9, 2026 adding anticipation; stock was ~$18.83 on May 29, 2026.
up.ten_day_catalyst: May 21 Claude Compliance API / Agentic Fabric AI-agent security launch plus a cluster of bullish analyst actions (Roth, Wells Fargo, Barclays PT to $22).

up.name: NETAPP INC
up.company_description: NetApp sells enterprise data-storage hardware/software (all-flash arrays, hybrid- and public-cloud storage) and earns recurring services/subscription revenue. GICS sector: Information Technology.
bullets: On 2026-05-28, NetApp reported fiscal Q4 FY26 adjusted EPS of $2.43 vs $2.27 consensus and revenue of $1.95B vs $1.87B consensus, a record FY26.
Shares jumped ~17-21% the next session (2026-05-29), rising from a $142.40 close on 2026-05-28 to about $179.89, with an intraday high near $192.83.
FY27 guidance was the bigger driver: revenue guided to $7.325B-$7.575B and EPS $8.70-$8.90, both ahead of Street expectations.
Q1 FY27 guidance also topped consensus, EPS $2.05-$2.15 vs $1.84 and revenue $1.75B-$1.90B vs $1.67B, fueled by all-flash and AI/hybrid-cloud demand.
Multiple analyst upgrades/positive ratings followed the print, reinforcing the rally through the rest of the window.
up.ten_day_catalyst: Fiscal Q4 FY26 earnings beat (2026-05-28) plus well-above-consensus FY27 guidance driven by AI/all-flash storage demand.

down.name: ZOOMINFO TECHNOLOGIES INC
down.company_description: GTM is ZoomInfo Technologies, selling subscription access to a B2B go-to-market intelligence/data platform for sales and marketing teams; Information Technology (application software).
bullets: [2026-05-11] Reported Q1 FY26 that beat near-term consensus but cut FY26 revenue guidance to $1.185B-$1.205B from ~$1.26B (~5% midpoint cut); Q2 guide of $301.5M came 2.8% below estimates.
[2026-05-12] Shares collapsed ~37% in premarket (from ~$6.04 to ~$3.80) on the guidance cut plus a surprise 20% workforce reduction with $45M-$60M restructuring charges.

[2026-05-12] Announced a structural pivot to consumption/hybrid pricing from seat-based subscriptions, which markets read as an admission of competitive weakness and near-term revenue unpredictability.
[2026-05-14] Mizuho downgraded GTM to Underperform; securities-law investigations were announced into the cut guidance and forecasting, pressuring the stock further.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Continued de-rate from the May 11-12 guidance cut, 20% layoffs, and pricing-model pivot, compounded by analyst downgrades and securities-law probes.

down.name: UBIQUITI INC
down.company_description: Ubiquiti designs and sells networking gear (UniFi, enterprise WiFi, routers, cameras) through a low-cost online distribution model; Information Technology / communications-equipment sector.
bullets: [2026-05-08] Reported FQ3 2026: revenue $788.2M and adjusted EPS $3.88, beating consensus (~$778M rev, ~$2.94 EPS), led by the Enterprise Technology segment.
[2026-05-08] Revenue fell sequentially from $814.9M in FQ2, and the release provided no forward guidance or FQ4/FY26 outlook, unsettling investors.
[2026-05-11] Shares dropped roughly 12-13% (to about $733.80) as the market focused on sequential revenue decline and the absence of guidance despite the headline beat.
[2026-05-11] Stock remained richly valued after a multi-quarter run, leaving it vulnerable to a de-rate once growth momentum visibly stalled.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Post-earnings de-rate as investors punished the sequential revenue decline and lack of forward guidance despite a Q3 beat.

down.name: GCI LIBERTY INC SERIES A
down.company_description: GLIBA is GCI Liberty Series A, the Alaska-focused broadband/wireless operator (GCI) spun off from Liberty Broadband in July 2025; Communication Services / telecom sector.
bullets: [2026-05-06] Reported Q1 2026: revenue slipped to $256M from $266M, net earnings fell to $18M from $35M, and Adjusted OIBDA dropped to $93M from $113M on weaker consumer/business data revenue.
[2026-05-06] EPS of $0.45 badly missed the $1.21 consensus (a $0.76 miss), with costs rising on distribution, technology, SBC and Quintillion acquisition expenses.
[2026-05-07] Series A shares fell ~16.1% the day after the print; subscriber trends were weak with broadband subs down 1,200 in the quarter amid SpaceX competition and a fiber line break.
[2026-05-14] Zacks downgraded GCI Liberty to Strong Sell, and shares (along with Series C GLIBK) ground to fresh 52-week lows later in May.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Ongoing fallout from the May 6 Q1 EPS miss and OIBDA decline, with downgrades and subscriber-loss concerns driving shares to new 52-week lows.

down.name: GCI LIBERTY INC SERIES C
down.company_description: GLIBK is GCI Liberty Series C, the non-voting share class of the same Alaska broadband/wireless operator (GCI) as GLIBA; Communication Services / telecom sector.
bullets: [2026-05-06] Same Q1 2026 print as GLIBA: revenue $256M (down from $266M), Adjusted OIBDA $93M (down from $113M), and EPS $0.45 versus $1.21 consensus, a $0.76 miss.
[2026-05-07] Series C shares hit a new one-year low on the disappointing earnings; the stock traded near $26.51 versus a prior close of $32.97.
[2026-05-07] Operational pressure included broadband subscribers down 1,200 (to 151,200) on mobile-only switching, limited SpaceX competition, and a fiber line break.
[2026-05-29] GLIBK hit a fresh 52-week low later in the month as negative sentiment persisted, with the 52-week range spanning roughly $25.33 to $41.18.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Same catalyst as GLIBA: persistent weakness from the May 6 Q1 EPS/OIBDA miss and downgrades pushing the Series C shares to new 52-week lows.

down.name: BULLISH
down.company_description: Bullish operates a regulated cryptocurrency exchange; earns trading fees and financial-services revenue. Recently expanding into blockchain-enabled equity transfer-agent services. GICS: Financials.
bullets: May 5, 2026 (day 1 of window): BLSH fell ~8.5% pre-market after announcing a $4.2B all-stock acquisition of Equiniti — $2.35B in BLSH shares priced at $38.48/share, heavily dilutive — setting the tone for the entire 20-day decline.
May 14, 2026: Q1 2026 results missed on both lines (EPS $0.13 vs $0.17 consensus; revenue $92.8M vs ~$95M expected), adding a fundamental growth concern layer to the dilution overhang.

Bitcoin fell from around $76K in mid-May to ~$67K by early June (approximately -12%), reducing exchange revenue expectations and weighting on BLSH throughout the period; spot BTC ETFs saw $2.30B in net outflows in May, the largest monthly outflow of 2026.

As of early June the stock sat ~38% below its May 4 reference price ($38.48) used to price the Equiniti deal, meaning acquirer stock is worth materially less than at announcement and raising questions about deal economics.
The Equiniti deal is not expected to close until January 2027, leaving a prolonged execution-risk and dilution-overhang period with no near-term accretion to offset the sentiment damage.
down.ten_day_catalyst: May 5 announcement of $4.2B all-stock Equiniti acquisition initiated the 20-day decline, compounded by Q1 earnings miss and weakening Bitcoin prices.

down.name: STRATEGY INC CLASS A
down.company_description: Strategy Inc (formerly MicroStrategy) holds ~843,000 Bitcoin on its balance sheet, funded via equity and debt issuance; operates as a leveraged Bitcoin treasury vehicle. GICS: Information Technology.
bullets: Bitcoin declined from roughly $80K in early May to ~$67K by June 3 (approximately -16%), directly eroding MSTR's NAV; as a leveraged BTC proxy MSTR typically amplifies Bitcoin drawdowns 1.5–2x.
Mid-May 2026: Strategy raised ~$2.03B via new STRC preferred shares and MSTR common stock issuance (selling 430,344 MSTR shares + 19.5M STRC shares) — ongoing equity dilution as Bitcoin stalled.

May 26–31: Strategy disclosed selling 801,994 common shares via ATM ($128.3M proceeds) AND 32 BTC (first BTC sale since 2022), a one-two punch of dilution and liquidity-stress signals in the same week.

BTC spot ETFs recorded $2.30B in net outflows in May 2026 — the largest monthly outflow of the year — indicating institutional de-risking that weighed on Bitcoin and correlated assets throughout the 20-day window.

Mizuho cut price target by ~20% to $265 (from $320) during the window, and analysts broadly flagged that Strategy's ~$1.7B annual preferred dividend obligation now exceeds its ~$871M cash buffer, creating structural refinancing risk.
down.ten_day_catalyst: 20-day decline driven by Bitcoin falling ~16% from ~$80K to ~$67K combined with repeated MSTR equity dilution via ATM offerings and first BTC sale since 2022.

down.name: COTY INC CLASS A
down.company_description: Global cosmetics and fragrance company; sells mass-market (CoverGirl, Rimmel) and prestige (Gucci Beauty, Burberry) beauty brands via retail and specialty channels. Consumer Staples.
bullets: May 6–7, 2026: Q1 FY2026 earnings disappointed — organic revenue fell ~7%, GAAP net loss of $0.03/share missed estimates by $0.02, and operating margin turned deeply negative at ~-29%.
Management cited European retailer inventory destocking, Middle East softness from geopolitical disruptions, and a highly promotional environment as primary headwinds.

Prior quarter: Coty had already withdrawn its full-year EBITDA guidance, announced a CEO transition, and faced securities class-action lawsuits related to these events — overhang from these catalysts persisted into the 20d window.

Stock fell ~6% on May 6 post-earnings, and continued sliding; COTY is down ~22.7% year-to-date and ~53.5% from its 52-week high of $5.17 (May 2025), trading around $2.13–$2.23 in late May/early June 2026.
Consumer Beauty segment revenues declined ~4% in the most recent quarter; prestige fragrance growth also decelerated, removing both pillars of the bull case simultaneously.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Q1 organic revenue -7% miss plus lingering CEO exit, withdrawn EBITDA guidance, and securities lawsuit overhang compressed the already-depressed stock further.

down.name: ZOETIS INC CLASS A
down.company_description: Zoetis is the largest pure-play animal health company, selling vet pharmaceuticals, vaccines, parasiticides and diagnostics for pets and livestock; Health Care sector.
bullets: [2026-05-07] Q1 2026 revenue ~$2.3B, roughly flat on an organic operational basis and a miss; stock fell ~21% on the print as competition and softer pet-owner spending bit.
[2026-05-07] Cut FY26 adjusted EPS guide to $6.85-$7.00 from $7.00-$7.10; new midpoint $6.93 sits below ~$7.03 consensus.
[2026-05-07] Lower Librela (OA-pain monoclonal antibody) sales plus generic competition on Convenia and Cerenia flagged as key drags.
[2026-05-08] Record ~$1.42B trading turnover as the de-rating extended, underscoring a structural-growth-narrative reset for the name.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Watch for analyst-day or KOL commentary on Librela competitive dynamics and whether the lowered FY26 guide proves a floor.

down.name: SAREPTA THERAPEUTICS INC
down.company_description: Sarepta develops gene and RNA therapies for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, including gene therapy Elevidys, earning revenue from product sales and royalties. GICS sector: Health Care.
bullets: Sarepta reported Q1 2026 results in May 2026 showing Elevidys net product sales of just $102M, down from a $375M record in Q1 2025.
Shares fell ~7-10% on the print as the steep Elevidys revenue decline overshadowed a headline EPS/revenue beat.
The sales collapse reflects FDA restricting Elevidys to ambulatory (walking) DMD patients after prior safety concerns and patient deaths, shrinking the addressable population.
Continued safety/label overhang and weak demand kept the stock under pressure across the window despite CEO Doug Ingram saying the portfolio had 'begun to stabilize.'
Net result was a ~-27.7% move over the 20d window as the demand miss reset growth expectations downward.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Q1 2026 print showed Elevidys sales crashing to $102M (from $375M YoY), confirming demand erosion under FDA ambulatory-only restriction.

down.name: WHIRLPOOL CORP
down.company_description: Whirlpool manufactures and sells major home appliances (washers, refrigerators, ranges) under brands like Whirlpool, Maytag and KitchenAid. GICS sector: Consumer Discretionary.
bullets: On 2026-05-07 Whirlpool reported Q1 with non-GAAP EPS of -$0.56 (missing by ~$1.03) and revenue of $3.27B vs $3.62B a year earlier, a net loss of $82M; shares fell ~16%.
On 2026-05-08 Whirlpool suspended its dividend for the first time since 2009 to conserve cash for debt repayment/restructuring, sending shares down a further ~12%.
FY guidance was cut sharply: revenue now seen down ~3% and adjusted EPS down 44%-52%, versus prior near-flat revenue and ~+12% EPS expectations.
Management flagged recession-level US industry decline as consumer confidence collapsed, with tariff/input-cost pressure compounding weak housing-led demand.
The stock kept sliding, hitting a 52-week low of $38.38 in late May, leaving the 20d window down ~-26.9%.
down.ten_day_catalyst: Q1 EPS/revenue miss (2026-05-07) plus first dividend suspension since 2009 (2026-05-08) and a deep guidance cut on recession-level appliance demand.
